prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A door handle for actuating a mortise lock of a door with an output shaft and a handle facing away from the door. The output shaft and the handle have a common rotation axis and are connected to one another via an electromechanical clutch. The output shaft has a recess, on the side facing the handle, dimensioned for a coupling element that is axially displaceable between open and closed positions with a motor, while the handle has a receptacle dimensioned to accommodate the coupling element opposite to the recess. The door handle is particularly reliable when the motor drives a coupling (auxiliary) shaft on which and/or in which at least one coil spring is disposed non-rotatably and coaxially with respect to the stator of the motor. The auxiliary shaft has at least one protrusion engaging in an intermediate space between two neighbored windings of the coil spring to displace the coil spring axially as a result of rotation of the auxiliary shaft. The coil spring engages with the coupling element to at least preload the coupling element, as a result of the axial displacement of the coil spring, in a direction corresponding to such displacement.

outputs.L1:
A door handle for actuating a mortise lock of a door comprises an output shaft and a handle facing away from the door. The output shaft and the handle share a common axis of rotation and are interconnected by an electromechanical clutch. On the side facing the handle, the output shaft includes a recess dimensioned to receive a coupling element that is axially displaceable by a motor between open and closed positions. The handle includes a receptacle positioned opposite the recess and dimensioned to accommodate the coupling element.

The door handle is particularly reliable in that the motor drives a coupling, or auxiliary, shaft on and/or in which at least one coil spring is disposed non-rotatably and coaxially with respect to the stator of the motor. The auxiliary shaft includes at least one protrusion that engages an intermediate space between two neighboring windings of the coil spring, thereby axially displacing the coil spring as the auxiliary shaft rotates. The coil spring engages the coupling element so as to at least preload the coupling element, as a result of the axial displacement of the coil spring, in a direction corresponding to that displacement.
outputs.L2:
A door handle is provided for operating a door’s mortise lock, the handle projecting away from the door and an output shaft being associated with it. The handle and the output shaft share the same axis of rotation and are joined together by an electromechanical clutch.

On the side directed toward the handle, the output shaft includes a recess sized to receive a coupling element. This coupling element can be shifted axially by a motor between an unlocked/open position and a locked/closed position. The handle also includes a receptacle positioned opposite the recess and shaped to receive the coupling element.

The door handle achieves especially dependable operation when the motor turns a coupling or auxiliary shaft. At least one coil spring is arranged on and/or within this auxiliary shaft so that it is coaxial with, and rotationally fixed relative to, the motor stator. The auxiliary shaft includes at least one projection that extends into the gap between two adjacent turns of the coil spring. When the auxiliary shaft rotates, this projection causes the coil spring to move in the axial direction. Through this axial movement, the coil spring acts on the coupling element and at least biases it in the same direction as the spring’s displacement.
outputs.L3:
The door handle assembly is configured to actuate a mortise lock by means of an output shaft and a handle that are arranged on a common axis of rotation. When the handle is operatively connected to the output shaft, rotation of the handle is transmitted to the output shaft, thereby enabling actuation of the mortise lock.

The connection between the handle and the output shaft is controlled by an electromechanical clutch. This clutch selectively couples or decouples the handle from the output shaft, allowing the lock to be placed in either an engaged state, in which the handle can operate the mortise lock, or a disengaged state, in which rotation of the handle is not transmitted to the output shaft.

The clutch includes a coupling element that is movable in an axial direction between an open position and a closed position. In the closed position, the coupling element engages both a recess formed in the output shaft and a corresponding receptacle formed in the handle. This engagement establishes a torque-transmitting connection between the handle and the output shaft. In the open position, the coupling element is withdrawn from at least one of these receiving formations, thereby interrupting the torque transmission path and preventing the handle from actuating the lock.

Axial movement of the coupling element is produced by a motor-driven mechanism. The motor drives an auxiliary shaft, which is provided with a coaxially arranged coil spring. The coil spring is mounted so that it is non-rotatable relative to the auxiliary shaft, while still being capable of axial displacement along the auxiliary shaft.

When the motor rotates the auxiliary shaft, the coil spring is displaced axially as a result of the shaft’s rotation. Depending on the direction of rotation, the coil spring is moved in one axial direction or the opposite axial direction. This axial displacement causes the coil spring to preload the coupling element toward the corresponding clutch position. As a result, the coupling element is urged either toward the closed position, in which the handle and output shaft are coupled, or toward the open position, in which the handle and output shaft are decoupled.
outputs.L4:
A door handle assembly for a mortise lock is provided with an electromechanical clutch that selectively connects or disconnects the handle from the lock-operating mechanism. The clutch includes a coupling element that can be shifted between a locked position, in which rotation of the handle is not transmitted to the lock, and an unlocked position, in which the handle is operatively connected so that the latch or lock mechanism can be actuated.

The axial movement of the coupling element is produced by a motor-driven auxiliary shaft. When the motor is energized, the auxiliary shaft rotates and acts on a coil spring arranged around or adjacent to the shaft. The coil spring cooperates with a protrusion, shoulder, or similar engagement feature so that rotation of the auxiliary shaft causes the spring to move axially or to apply an axial preload. This axial force is then transferred to the coupling element, shifting it into or out of engagement with the corresponding clutch component.

In one operating state, the spring urges the coupling element into a position where the handle is coupled to the mortise lock mechanism, allowing the user to open the door by turning the handle. In the other operating state, the coupling element is displaced or held away from engagement, so that the handle can rotate freely or without operating the lock. The motor may be controlled by an electronic access system, such as a keypad, card reader, wireless receiver, biometric reader, or other authorization device.

The use of a coil spring and protrusion-based axial actuation mechanism improves the reliability of the clutch. The spring can compensate for small manufacturing tolerances, wear, misalignment, or impact loads, while still applying a consistent force to the coupling element. Because the coupling element is shifted or preloaded in the axial direction rather than relying solely on direct rigid displacement, the mechanism is less likely to jam and can maintain dependable engagement even after repeated use.

As a result, the door handle provides a compact and durable electromechanical clutch arrangement suitable for mortise locks. The motor-driven auxiliary shaft, coil spring, and coupling element cooperate to provide controlled locking and unlocking of the handle, while the spring-assisted actuation enhances the dependability of clutch engagement and improves the overall service life of the lock assembly.

**The Importance of “The” in English**

“The” is one of the most common and important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, which means it is used to refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, in the sentence “Please close the door,” the word “the” tells us that the speaker is talking about a particular door, not just any door.

Although “the” is a small word, it plays a big role in communication. It helps make sentences clearer and more precise. Without it, many sentences can sound incomplete or confusing. For example, “I saw the movie” means the speaker and listener likely know which movie is being discussed, while “I saw a movie” refers to any movie.

“The” is also used with unique things, such as “the sun,” “the moon,” and “the Earth.” It can appear before singular nouns, plural nouns, and uncountable nouns, depending on the meaning of the sentence.

In short, “the” may be simple, but it is essential. It helps speakers and writers point to specific things and create meaning clearly in English.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an electromechanical door handle with a mortise lock, clutch, axially movable coupling element, motor-driven auxiliary shaft, and coil spring preload mechanism.
counterfactuals.output: An electromechanical door handle assembly includes a mortise lock having a latch-operating follower, a handle-operated shaft, and a clutch mechanism selectively coupling the handle-operated shaft to the follower. An axially movable coupling element is arranged between the handle-operated shaft and the follower and is displaceable between an engaged position, in which rotation of the handle is transmitted to the mortise lock to retract a latch, and a disengaged position, in which the handle rotates without operating the latch. A motor-driven auxiliary shaft is configured to actuate the clutch mechanism by moving the coupling element axially. A coil spring preload mechanism biases the coupling element toward one of the engaged and disengaged positions and stores mechanical preload energy to assist movement of the coupling element when the motor-driven auxiliary shaft is actuated. The arrangement enables electrically controlled locking and unlocking of the door handle while permitting compact integration with a mortise lock and reliable clutch engagement under varying handle positions and load conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention described in this patent claim: a door handle with an output shaft and handle sharing a rotation axis, connected by an electromechanical clutch, where a motor moves a coupling element using a coaxial coil spring on an auxiliary shaft.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a door handle assembly in which the handle and an output shaft rotate about the same axis but are selectively connected by an electromechanical clutch.

A motor controls a movable coupling element that can engage or disengage the handle from the output shaft. When engaged, turning the handle rotates the output shaft to operate the door lock or latch. When disengaged, the handle can turn without driving the output shaft, preventing unauthorized opening.

The motor drives the coupling element through an auxiliary shaft fitted with a coaxial coil spring, which helps transmit or bias the movement needed to shift the clutch between its locked and unlocked states. This provides an electrically controlled handle mechanism, suitable for electronic access control doors.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical description of a reliable motorized door handle for actuating a mortise lock, including the recess, receptacle, coupling element, auxiliary shaft, protrusion, and coil spring arrangement.
counterfactuals.output:
A motorized door handle assembly for actuating a mortise lock includes a handle body having an internal recess that houses a drive mechanism. A receptacle is formed in the recess and is configured to receive and support a coupling element operatively connected to the lock follower of the mortise lock. The coupling element transmits rotation from the handle to the lock mechanism while permitting controlled motor-driven engagement or disengagement.

An auxiliary shaft is mounted within the handle body and extends through or adjacent to the receptacle. The auxiliary shaft is coupled to a motor output and is arranged to rotate the coupling element when powered. The coupling element includes a protrusion received in a corresponding guide portion of the receptacle so that rotation and axial positioning of the coupling element are constrained and reliably aligned with the mortise lock.

A coil spring is disposed around the auxiliary shaft or between the coupling element and the receptacle. The coil spring biases the coupling element toward a predetermined engagement position, maintaining consistent contact with the lock follower and compensating for tolerance variations, wear, or minor misalignment. This spring-loaded arrangement ensures reliable return, smooth torque transfer, and dependable actuation of the mortise lock by either manual handle movement or motorized operation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for a smart door handle in which a motor-driven auxiliary shaft axially displaces a coil spring to preload a coupling element between an output shaft recess and a handle receptacle.
counterfactuals.output: A smart door handle assembly includes a handle, an output shaft operably connectable to a latch or lock mechanism, and an electromechanical coupling arrangement selectively coupling the handle to the output shaft. The output shaft includes a recess aligned with a receptacle of the handle for receiving a coupling element. A motor drives an auxiliary shaft configured to axially displace a coil spring, thereby selectively preloading the coupling element toward an engaged position in which the coupling element is seated between the output shaft recess and the handle receptacle to transmit torque from the handle to the output shaft. Upon motor actuation in an opposite direction, the auxiliary shaft reduces or releases the spring preload to permit disengagement of the coupling element, decoupling the handle from the output shaft. The assembly enables electronically controlled locking and unlocking while retaining a compact mechanical preload structure suitable for integration within a door handle.
